dossier.architecture: Differential drive with simple two-position launcher and tilting telescopic climb.

subsystems.intake: Collector has large printed mecanum ends; biased flaps and tread combat two-ball jams.
subsystems.transfer: Tall conveyor and rejection fork; infrared staging pauses a ball long enough for delayed color sensing.
subsystems.scoring: Two-position pneumatic elevation at fixed speed/distance; brass flywheel inertia and compliant passive Lexan/yoga-mat hood. Powered back roller was unfinished.
subsystems.endgame: Tilting telescope with passive hooks and rope-induced center-of-gravity movement; lighter plastic outer stage outperformed a heavier replacement that damaged bearings.
subsystems.controls: Color rejection disabled in autonomous to save time, enabled in teleop. Limited field practice informed simpler shot controls.

versions: Heavier aluminum climb stage was tried and rejected; do not describe it as the final improvement.
dossier.analysis: This is a valuable counterexample to copying the most complex elite architecture: development time and practice availability can make a discrete shot map and lower mechanical mass more effective.
limits: Only the reviewed published configurations are established; intermediate changes may be undocumented.

context_documents.title: 2022-694 · Sensor latency and passive hood compliance are deliberate constraints
context_documents.body:
# 2022-694: Sensor latency and passive hood compliance are deliberate constraints

Focused study supplement. Not a full binder/CAD review, exhaustive subsystem specification, every-version history or visual interview watch.

## Published / retained construction account

A tall conveyor and rejection fork pause cargo for delayed color sensing. Printed collector contacts and biased flaps address two-ball jams. The retained launcher uses added flywheel inertia and a compliant passive hood; an additional powered back roller was unfinished.

## Team-stated reasoning or boundary

The team explicitly prioritizes simpler scoring after pandemic-related experience gaps.

## Engineering interpretation — analyst inference

A deliberate staging pause can improve correct classification even when it lowers nominal feed speed. A passive hood saves actuation but must hold repeatable compression as material wears. Unfinished hardware cannot be credited as an explanation of observed shooting.

## Proposed validation — not performed

Measure classification latency, false rejection, two-ball recovery and trajectory drift as the hood material ages.

## Limits

Focused technical passages and the retained dossier are the evidence scope. Exact event installation, complete CAD tolerances and all intermediate revisions are not certified.

source_reviews.title: Behind the Bumpers with StuyPulse at IRI
source_reviews.locator: 1:18–2:48 intake; 2:48–5:13 branch and sensing; 5:18–9:17 shooter and calibration; 9:31–11:52 climb
source_reviews.review_basis: Read the full available English automatic caption track, including the start and end. Technical details are attributed to team speakers. No visual inspection claimed.
facts: The single-pivot pneumatic intake uses several roller styles and added flaps with asymmetric tread to reduce simultaneous-ball jams.
A bump and branch separate the reject path from the tall feed. Infrared detection pauses the cargo for color sensing.
The printed two-piece hood uses a Lexan liner and compliant padding. The team focused calibration on repeatable shot locations.
source_reviews.limitations: Automatic captions badly garble the team name in places. The recorded technical answers and video identifier are used. Shot accuracy and material durability are team reports.

source_review.whole_robot_explanation: StuyPulse chose a differential-drive scorer with a compact number of calibrated shots. Its tall launcher was partly a consequence of the cargo branch below it: a ball could continue through the reject path or rise to shoot. The mechanical system used printed, plastic and wood parts in specific jobs, with compliant backing used to tolerate cargo variation and a flexible climb stage reported to tolerate swing.
piece_flow: Outside wheels funnel cargo past the intake plates. Asymmetric flap/tread contact favors one ball when two reach the throat.
A belt couples intake and conveyor. At the branch, an IR sensor stops the ball briefly so the color sensor can make a decision.
Unwanted cargo goes straight out and desired cargo rises to the feed roller, shooter flywheel and two-position hood.
source_review.packaging_and_motion: The branch needs height for the accepted route while keeping the reject outlet open. That sets launcher height and the space left beside the climb. The chassis supplies shot yaw, and the team spent tuning time on a small shooting envelope rather than a dense field-wide speed map.

subsystems.name: Piston intake and passive singulation
subsystems.construction: Piston-actuated intake, printed edge contacts larger than their plates, inner funneling contacts and later flaps with asymmetric tread.
subsystems.operation: Bias one of two adjacent balls into the single path first.
subsystems.team_rationale: The team wanted a simple primary scorer and added the flaps after observing paired jams.
subsystems.engineering_analysis: Deliberate asymmetry can do the work of a powered agitator when the resulting lead persists until the throat captures one ball.
subsystems.interfaces: The intake and conveyor are belt-coupled, making continued drive relevant to both acquisition and rejection.
subsystems.service_and_failure_modes: Compare pairs entering from either side and inspect printed contacts and flap tread after wear.

subsystems.name: Color branch
subsystems.construction: Conveyor bump, straight rejection outlet, rising score path, REV color sensor and IR trigger.
subsystems.operation: Stop cargo at the reader briefly, classify it, and route it before the coupled conveyor drives it out.
subsystems.team_rationale: The delay avoided ejecting alliance cargo. The team generally disabled the feature in auto because it consumed time.
subsystems.engineering_analysis: The default physical trajectory matters during a late decision. Evaluate whether a missing read causes rejection, blocking or scoring.
subsystems.interfaces: Stopping the coupled drive pauses new intake while the ball is sampled.
subsystems.service_and_failure_modes: Try mixed pairs, a slow sensor and reflection changes, then time the next good shot.
subsystems.unknowns: Exact dwell and branch geometry not established.

subsystems.name: Fixed launcher
subsystems.construction: Two-part printed hood with Lexan liner and compliant mat backing, feeder roller, brass flywheel inertia and piston angle change.
subsystems.operation: Drive to a calibrated pose, bring the ball to speed and release using the close or farther shot configuration.
subsystems.team_rationale: Limited calibration resources favored repeatable presets. The team used compliant padding for variation in ball inflation.
subsystems.engineering_analysis: Padding and added inertia can help repeatability, but check shot sensitivity after compression set and quantify recovery under rapid feeds.
subsystems.interfaces: The differential drive supplies yaw and camera/encoder fusion supports the set shot.
subsystems.service_and_failure_modes: Test unevenly inflated balls and loss of pose confidence. Inspect the seam and liner after repeated launches.
subsystems.unknowns: No measured exit speed or verified launch-pad accuracy.

subsystems.name: Tilting telescope
subsystems.construction: Telescoping active arm, passive hooks, plastic outer stage, reported wood reinforcement and a rope for small attitude change.
subsystems.operation: Catch a bar, settle onto passive hooks, tilt and reach the next.
subsystems.team_rationale: An aluminum substitution reportedly reduced flex and damaged bearings during swing.
subsystems.engineering_analysis: That failure suggests evaluating side-load and binding through the swing before changing stiffness. It does not establish a general preferred material.
subsystems.interfaces: Reach depends on the real suspended attitude and available clearance.
subsystems.service_and_failure_modes: Fixture-test one-sided load and bearing damage after repeated swing.

revisions: Added anti-jam flaps and tread. The team describes an unsuccessful aluminum outer-stage trial and a later additional shooting position.
transferable_principles: Use a piece-present sensor to buy classification time deliberately.
Concentrate shot calibration where the drive team can return consistently.
disconfirming_conditions: Long travel to a few shooting locations can erase calibration savings.
A flexible climb member can fail if load or alignment requires controlled stiffness.
remaining_gaps: Exact IRI competition code, branch dimensions and fatigue measurements.
recommended_images: Request side images of the branch and the printed hood liner, then the climb outer stage and passive hooks.
